tagline: An old southern port town with a Malay soul — historic mosques, a Sino-Portuguese old quarter, and bold local food
introHtml:
Pattani is an old port town on the Gulf of Thailand that was once the Sultanate of Patani. People remember it for the Malay character that mixes with Chinese and Thai influences all in one town — the ancient brick ruins of Krue Se Mosque, the big Pattani Central Mosque, and the Anoru old quarter, where Sino-Portuguese shophouses still line the street.

Outside town there are long sandy beaches like Talo Kapo Beach and Laem Ta Chi, mangrove forests at the river mouth, and a fishing way of life that's still busy. The food here is bold southern Thai mixed with Malay — khao yam, nasi dagae, sticky rice with kai kolae, and tea shops that open early. People come to Pattani for the old town, Malay culture, and local dishes you'd struggle to find anywhere else.
bestTime: February–May, clear skies and little rain — good for walking the old town and the beaches. November–January is monsoon season with heavy rain and rough surf.

highlights.name: Krue Se Mosque
highlights.blurb: The centuries-old brick mosque left unfinished — the first image that comes to mind when people think of Pattani. The legend of Lim Ko Niao is tied to this spot too.

highlights.name: Pattani Central Mosque
highlights.blurb: The big mosque in the middle of town and the spiritual heart of the local Muslim community. The dome and minaret architecture is striking, a reminder that Muslim life is the backbone of this province.

highlights.name: Anoru–Kudi Old Quarter
highlights.blurb: An old-town street still lined with Sino-Portuguese buildings and old wooden houses. The Leng Chu Kiang shrine of Lim Ko Niao is here — wander the old buildings and soak up the story of the former port town.

highlights.name: Lim Ko Niao Shrine (Leng Chu Kiang)
highlights.blurb: An old Chinese shrine in the center of town, revered by the local Chinese community. The fire-walking and goddess procession during Chinese New Year draws the whole province.

highlights.name: Talo Kapo Beach and Laem Ta Chi
highlights.blurb: A long sandy beach on the Gulf of Thailand with the Laem Ta Chi sandspit reaching out to sea. There are fishing villages and brightly painted kolae boats — a spot for sea views and Pattani's coastal life.

highlights.name: Fishing life and kolae boats
highlights.blurb: Pattani is an old fishing town with brightly patterned kolae boats along the coast, reflecting the craft and Malay culture you can still see in the seaside villages.

foodScene.name: Khao yam (southern rice salad)
foodScene.note: Rice tossed with budu sauce, shredded vegetables, toasted coconut, dried shrimp, and herbs — sour, salty, and sweet in one plate. A light breakfast that people in Pattani eat all the time.

foodScene.name: Nasi dagae
foodScene.note: Rice cooked with coconut milk, served with Malay-style fish or chicken curry, eaten with egg and chili paste. A quick breakfast sold at markets and tea shops all over town.

foodScene.name: Sticky rice with kai kolae
foodScene.note: Grilled chicken brushed with a sweet-salty coconut sauce scented with Malay spices, eaten with sticky rice or plain rice. A signature local dish of the deep south.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Tai pla curry, yellow curry, khua kling, and stir-fried sator beans, eaten with hot rice and fresh raw vegetables. A bold home-style meal you can find all over town.

foodScene.name: Gulf of Thailand seafood
foodScene.note: Pattani is a fishing town with shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fresh fish. Seafood spots grill, steam, stir-fry with curry powder, and make tom yum — ingredients straight off the boats.

foodScene.name: Roti and tea at Muslim shops
foodScene.note: Tea shops open from morning till late. Roti, crisp outside and soft inside, eaten with curry or drizzled with condensed milk, with pulled tea and old-style coffee. Sitting at a tea shop is part of life in this town.

foodScene.name: Budu and fish chili paste
foodScene.note: Budu is the deep south's signature fermented fish sauce, used as the dressing for khao yam and to make budu chili paste eaten with fresh vegetables and fried fish — a local taste Pattani people grow up with.

foodScene.name: Malay traditional sweets
foodScene.note: Malay-style sweets like akok, putu kedeng, and colorful coconut-milk desserts, sold at morning markets and night markets. Eaten with hot tea as a snack through the day.

attractions.name: Krue Se Mosque
attractions.blurb: The ancient brick mosque left unfinished — a historic monument of Pattani tied to the legend of Lim Ko Niao. Stop to see the architecture and hear the story.

attractions.name: Pattani Central Mosque
attractions.blurb: The province's big mosque in the heart of town, with a graceful dome and minaret. The spiritual heart of the Muslim community and a landmark people stop to photograph.

attractions.name: Anoru Old Quarter
attractions.blurb: An old-town street still lined with Sino-Portuguese buildings and old wooden houses. Wander the old buildings and cafes and take in the feel of Pattani's former port town.

attractions.name: Leng Chu Kiang Shrine
attractions.blurb: The old Chinese shrine of Lim Ko Niao, revered by the local Chinese community. The goddess procession and fire-walking during Chinese New Year light up the whole province.

attractions.name: Talo Kapo Beach
attractions.blurb: A long sandy beach on the Gulf of Thailand with fishing villages and brightly painted kolae boats — a spot for sea views, resting by the shore, and watching Pattani's coastal life.

attractions.name: Laem Ta Chi
attractions.blurb: A sandspit reaching out to sea at the mouth of the Pattani River, with a quiet beach, mangroves, and small-scale fishing. Good for taking in the views and photographing the sea on both sides.

attractions.name: Sai Khao Waterfall National Park
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered waterfall in the hills of Khok Pho district — clear, cool water with short hikes and swimming. Wat Sai Khao is nearby. A popular nature spot in the province.

attractions.name: Ao Manao Skywalk
attractions.blurb: A viewing walkway reaching out over the sea and mangroves around Ao Manao, looking out over the beach and fishing boats. A spot for a stroll in the sea breeze close to town.
